title: Parastichy numbers change when the structure varies greatly in size

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Parastichy numbers change when the structure varies greatly in size

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Phyllotactic parastichy numbers vary with the size of the whole structure, as in sunflower discs where one species may show 34/55, 55/89 or even 89/144 rows.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIV: On Leaf-Arrangement, or Phyllotaxis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The arrangement, as we have seen, is apt to vary when the entire structure varies greatly in size, as in the disc of the sunflower.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XIV, “On Leaf-Arrangement, or Phyllotaxis”; topic “Numbers of parastichies”. Scope: sunflower capitula and other composite inflorescences

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch14-05: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.80

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Both disc size and row counts can be extracted from existing images with standard methods. Adequate within-species replication can directly test the predicted association and listed transitions.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure capitulum diameter and parastichy count pairs across sunflower heads within and among species, then model count transitions with size while controlling developmental stage. Positive, ordered transitions such as 34/55 to 55/89 to 89/144 support the claim; size-independent counts refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Size and developmental stage are correlated.

Very dense high-order spirals require high-resolution images.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.96
data adequacy: 0.62
discriminating power: 0.88
analysis feasibility: 0.82
data existence: 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Size-dependent parastichy number is the pattern the sunflower study was built to capture, and both the counts and the images needed to measure disc size are public. Hundreds of heads span the Fibonacci pairs Thompson lists. Other composites are not in the file, but the stated example, and the scope centered on sunflower discs, can be confirmed or refuted directly.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure disc diameter on the annotated sunflower images and test whether parastichy pairs (34/55, 55/89, 89/144 and others) shift upward with size. The claim is confirmed by an ordered increase of both counts with diameter; it is refuted if pair identity is independent of size or if small heads systematically carry the higher pairs.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The file is one cultivated species, whereas the claim also mentions other composite heads in passing.

Some heads are too disordered for a single pair to be assigned.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.86
analysis feasibility: 0.85
data adequacy: 0.74
operationalizability: 0.9
discriminating power: 0.8

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: Within one species of sunflower, larger capitula carry higher parastichy pairs: head diameter increases in order across the successive Fibonacci pairs (e.g. 21/34 < 34/55 < 55/89 < 89/144), so parastichy numbers rise with the size of the whole structure.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: fetch.py obtains the two spreadsheets (Dryad serves downloads behind a browser proof-of-work challenge; files were fetched with headless Chrome, checksummed, and a 49 KB derived table committed under derived/). analysis.py keeps heads with a reported head diameter and an adjacent Fibonacci-type pair (photoreviewed counts first, submitter counts otherwise), computes the Spearman correlation between diameter and the larger parastichy number, and compares median diameters across the main-sequence pair classes 21/34, 34/55, 55/89 and 89/144 (Kruskal-Wallis as a supplementary test).

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. In the Turing's Sunflowers data (Helianthus annuus), restrict to heads with a recorded head (seedhead) diameter and with both parastichy counts forming an adjacent pair of a Fibonacci-type sequence (Fibonacci, Lucas, double Fibonacci or F4, as defined by Swinton et al. 2016). The Spearman rank correlation between head diameter and the larger parastichy number must be positive with rho >= 0.30 and P < 0.01, and the median head diameter must increase monotonically across successive pair classes of the main Fibonacci sequence that each have n >= 10 heads.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. rho <= 0.10, or P >= 0.05, or an inversion of median diameter between adjacent main-sequence pair classes each with n >= 10 (larger pair at smaller heads). 0.10 < rho < 0.30 with P < 0.05 and no inversion is 'mixed'. If the data file carries no head-size measurement, the verdict is 'inconclusive' with reason 'data-unavailable'; if fewer than 50 heads have both diameter and a resolved pair, 'inconclusive' with reason 'underpowered'.

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: Spearman rho, head diameter (cm) vs larger parastichy number

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Thompson's 'size of the entire structure' is mapped to the diameter of the sunflower seedhead as reported by the grower; 'the arrangement' is mapped to the adjacent Fibonacci-type parastichy pair, ordered by its larger member. Primary counts are the photoreviewed counts where available, otherwise the submitter's counts. The claim's extension to other composites is not tested here; only the sunflower disc, which is Thompson's named example, is.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value: Data from: Novel Fibonacci and non-Fibonacci structure in the sunflower: results of a citizen science experiment (Turing's Sunflowers)

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
Head diameter was measured and reported by the growers themselves (citizen science), with unknown precision and probably mixed conventions (disc versus whole head); such noise biases the correlation towards zero, not away from it.

The sample is cultivated Helianthus annuus of many cultivars; the claim's remark about other composites is not tested.

Thompson lists 34/55, 55/89 and 89/144 as occurring in one species; here the 89/144 class has only 11 heads, though their median diameter (24 cm) is well above the 55/89 class (14 cm).

Size and developmental stage are confounded in a cross-sectional sample; the claim is about size, and that is what was measured.
